results.title: Why inter‑annotator agreement is critical to best‑in‑class gen AI training
results.content: While traditional accuracy metrics once ruled annotation evaluation, **inter‑annotator agreement (IAA)** has become the centerpiece of quality assurance in generative AI workflows. IAA measures how consistently multiple annotators label the same content. * **Cohen’s κ**: Used for two annotators on categorical tasks, adjusting for chance agreement. * **Krippendorff’s α**: Handles multiple annotators, missing data, ordinal or free‑text labels. Framed as a general standard for annotation tasks in generative AI. There’s a fundamental reason: when annotators interpret tone, narrative coherence, or meaning, **thoughtful disagreement** reflects task complexity — not laziness. ## Measuring IAA in generative AI workflows. For complex generative tasks (e.g., semantic similarity, reasoning), human IAA averages between **α = 0.68 – 0.76** across domains like accuracy, similarity or goal alignment, which closely matches LLM‑LLM agreement under controlled setups. 1. **Quality Detection**: Low IAA flags ambiguous guidelines or label definitions. 3. **Feedback Loops**: Used correctly, IAA becomes a continuous feedback mechanism — annotators meet, discuss disagreements, refine labels, and re‑calibrate guidelines mid‑project. 4. **Expert Credibility**: Expert annotators — versus crowdsourced raters — consistently show higher IAA in subjective tasks like coherence or style, reinforcing Sigma’s curated workforce advantage. ## How to raise IAA in annotation programs. Pilot IAA assessments help validate training clarity and label granularity. In annotation for generative and agentic AI, the error isn’t always human. IAA transforms disagreement from chaos into insight, serving as a compass for annotation quality and workflow design. High Inter-Annotator Agreement is achieved by cultivating a highly skilled and aligned workforce. results.title: Inter-Annotator Agreement: An Introduction to Cohen’s Kappa Statistic | by Surge AI | Medium
results.content: As starving aspiring novelists, Alix and Bob were both happy to moonlight as data labelers grading student essays. The raters also rarely disagreed about which essays were good: if Alix passed a student, Bob did too 86 / 94 = 91% of the time. In this case, it’s not clear which, if any, rater is objectively correct, so we can arbitrarily define this as the number of students Alix passed and Bob failed. Cohen’s kappa ranges from 1, representing perfect agreement between raters, to -1, meaning the raters choose different labels for every sample. Alix and Bob could easily achieve a Cohen’s kappa of 1 if they were both so lazy they decided to just auto-pass every single essay. Similarly, negative values for Cohen’s kappa don’t automatically mean that one of the raters is low-quality. Even for tasks that require consistency, low Cohen’s kappa values may reflect ambiguous instructions or inherently subjective questions (what makes an essay good anyway?) rather than rater error.

results.title: Inter-Annotator Agreement (IAA)
results.content: # Inter-Annotator Agreement (IAA). * Inter-annotator Agreement (IAA) is a statistical measure that quantifies the consistency among human annotators using metrics such as Cohen’s κ and Krippendorff’s α. Inter-annotator Agreement (IAA) is the fundamental statistical and methodological construct quantifying consistency among human annotators engaged in labeling, segmenting, or otherwise providing structured judgments over datasets. * Routine reporting of both **inter-** and **intra-annotator agreement**; intra-annotator agreement tracks label stability over time and isolates causes of low IAA due to subjective variance versus ambiguity or guideline inadequacy (Abercrombie et al., 2023). **Worker reliability weighting**: By leveraging inter-annotator and intra-annotator agreement, frameworks such as EffiARA compute annotator reliability scores used to re-weight samples during model training, directly improving downstream classifier performance—especially in low-agreement or subjective tasks (Cook et al., 2024). * **Multi-faceted reporting:** Combine intra-annotator agreement with IAA to dissect stability versus reliability and employ diagnostic matrices that distinguish subjectivity from ambiguity (Abercrombie et al., 2023). 4.
